text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm drafting an "envelope + KMS" ops playbook. Need agreement on DEK caching TTLs, RBAC roles for unwrap vs rotate, cross-cloud API differences, and an incident containment flow if a KEK is suspected compromised. Can we align here before I formalize?

alex: Short version: KEKs never leave KMS in plaintext. Generate or derive DEKs, persist only ciphertext, and cache plaintext DEKs in memory only for short periods. Prefer lazy rewraps to avoid big batch jobs.

raj: RBAC breakdown idea:
- service-decrypt-role: only kms:Decrypt / unwrapKey + DescribeKey. No rotate or key policy management.
- rewrap-role: allowed to Encrypt/GenerateDataKey/Encrypt (or ReEncrypt equivalent) — used only by rotation/rewrap jobs.
- key-admin-role: manage key policy + ListKeyVersions, gated behind approval + MFA.
Least-privilege: don't give any single principal both rotate and admin rights. Audit all role changes.

sam: Caching pattern suggestion: per-instance in-memory DEK cache keyed by (ciphertext_hash, key_version). Two-tier TTL: soft TTL 2m (async refresh) and hard TTL 45m (evict). On soft expiry, kick off an async refresh from KMS but keep serving with current DEK to avoid blocking.

maria: Why not a single TTL?

sam: Soft/hard gives us proactive refresh without dropping in-flight requests; reduces synchronous KMS pressure while bounding exposure window.

raj: Cross-cloud specifics:
- AWS: use GenerateDataKey to get plaintext DEK once and ciphertext_blob to store. Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/DescribeKey are core APIs. Watch per-account/region KMS quotas.
- GCP: Cloud KMS uses CryptoKey versions; often you call Encrypt to wrap a locally generated DEK (no direct GenerateDataKey parity). Track version IDs.
- Azure: Key Vault wrapKey/unwrapKey and key versions; use the key version id in metadata.
Always store key_version with ciphertext so services know exactly which key to call.

maria: KMS call volume concerns during spikes (deploys, rotation)?

sam: Mitigations: client-side token-bucket rate limiter, jittered exponential backoff on errors, per-region quotas, and a circuit-breaker that returns a controlled error so callers can degrade gracefully. Also, stagger rotations (shard-by-shard) and prefer lazy, on-access rewraps to spread load.

sec-bot: [automated] KMS API usage alert: region-us-east-1 2025-05-02T14:12:30Z (spike).

raj: Audit log guidance: record all KMS API calls (Decrypt/Encrypt/GenerateDataKey), cache hits/misses, rewrap job actions, and IAM changes. Attach correlation_id and user/role to every log line. Ship to SIEM with immutable retention >= 12 months.

sam: Metrics & alerts: unwrap_latency_p95, unwrap_error_rate, cache_hit_ratio. Alert thresholds: unwrap_error_rate > 0.5% for 5m, unwrap_latency_p95 > 200ms, sudden jump in Decrypt API QPS from baseline.

maria: Draft incident flow proposal (compact):
1) Detect — alerts on abnormal Decrypt volume, repeated 429/Throttling from KMS, or unexpected key-admin API calls.
2) Contain — disable specific key version (set disabled) or update key policy to deny decrypt.
3) Invalidate caches — publish internal "kms.invalidate:{keyid}:{version}" to pubsub; services evict matching DEKs immediately.
4) Recover/rewrap — run rewrap job under rewrap-role or lazy rewrap on first access (lazy preferred at scale).
5) Audit & notify — pull KMS audit logs + IAM change history, notify infosec/legal and execs.

alex: Practical rotation knobs: dual-unwrap window (accept old+new versions for configurable window), embed key_version in ciphertext metadata, and prefer lazy rewrap to reduce sudden KMS load. Only fully disable old version after monitoring drains.

sam: Example invalidation pattern we use elsewhere:

// rotation job
pubsub.publish("kms.invalidate", { key_id: "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123:key/abcd", new_version: "v3", ts: "2025-05-02T22:00:00Z" })

// service
onMessage(m) { if (m.key_id === cached.keyId) cached.evict() }

raj: Minimal AWS IAM snippet for service-decrypt-role (illustrative only):
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/abcd-ef01"
    }
  ]
}

maria: Note: restrict ListKeyVersions tightly — it leaks rotation cadence. Gate with approval and audit.

oncall: Add to oncall checklist (commands we will run):
- rdwctl kms disable-key --key-id <id> --version <v>
- rdwctl cache flush --selector "key:arn:aws:kms:..."
- rdwctl rewrap run --rate 1000/s --parallel 5
- verify SIEM for Decrypt/Disable events and IAM changes

sam: Dev/QA notes: provide a staging harness that forces rotation and validates cache invalidation + lazy rewrap under simulated load. Avoid using prod KEKs in dev.

maria: I'll draft the playbook with these sections plus emergency CLI snippets, IAM templates (parameterized), test plan, and a short timeline for rotation. Will post draft in #eng-security for review by EOD tomorrow.

rot-bot: [automated] scheduled rotation: alias/rdw-prod-enc -> v7 @ 2025-05-10T04:00:00Z

maria: Thanks everyone — please ping me directly if you want specific wording for the incident notification templates or legal blurb.
